Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • Two-month history of escalating workplace-related anxiety, morning dread, palpitations, insomnia (sleep 3–4 h/night), fatigue, anhedonia.  
  • New irregular palpitations lasting 2–10 min, accompanied by perceived rapid heartbeat; chest pain denied then partially affirmed (conflict noted).  
  • No prior similar episodes; no panic attacks yet.  
- Relevant family medical history:
  • Mother has a history of depression.  
  • Other family history not recorded.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • None reported.  
- Immunisation status reviewed:
  • Not recorded.  
- Sexual and reproductive health:
  • Not discussed.  
- Physical activity and nutrition:
  • Previously enjoyed running and tennis; currently reduced participation due to anxiety and fatigue.  
  • Diet unchanged apart from increased chocolate intake; eating regularly.  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  • Alcohol: binge drinking most Fridays/Saturdays (acknowledges exceeding limits) plus “a glass of wine” on some weekdays; exact units not recorded.  
  • Tobacco: occasional smoker.  
  • Recreational drugs: denies use.  
- Hearing loss or concerns:
  • Not recorded.  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):
  • Persistent low mood and anxiety; no suicidal thoughts or self-harm intent.  
  • Good family support; lives with parents.  
- Vision problems or recent changes:
  • Not recorded.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:
  • Lives with both parents; good support system.  
  • Avoiding friends/social activities secondary to anxiety and fatigue.

Management Plan

- Provided patient with NHS self-referral link for talking therapy (CBT) and online anxiety resources.  
- Discussed sleep hygiene materials; to be added to patient notes.  
- Recommended basic blood tests; patient to arrange via support line.  
- Advised GP follow-up one week after blood tests to review results and reassess anxiety/palpitations.  
- Discussed possibility of medication for anxiety if symptoms worsen or non-pharmacological measures ineffective.  
- Safety-netting: patient to call back if anxiety escalates, function deteriorates, or coping becomes difficult.

Consider:
  • Mental health care plan / psychologist referral if symptoms persist.  
  • Lifestyle counselling for alcohol reduction and smoking cessation.  
  • Preventive health check (BP, BMI, vaccinations) at next visit.  
  • CTG registration (if Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander status confirmed; not stated in transcript).  

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected: BP, pulse, weight/BMI, waist, immunisation history, past medical history, allergy status, cervical screening status, STI screen, blood sugar/lipid profile, urinalysis, hearing/vision checks.  
● Internal contradictions: Patient initially denied chest pain with palpitations but later stated it is “painful when my heart is beating fast” (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor speech overlaps and incomplete sentences but adequate for clinical documentation.
